explanation.text:
(Pro. 14:1-35)

Every wise, etc.--literally, "The wisdoms" (compare Pro 9:1) "of women," plural, a distributive form of speech.

buildeth . . . house--increases wealth, which the foolish, by mismanagement, lessen.

bsb.text: Every wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands.

explanation.text: uprightness--is the fruit of fearing God, as falsehood and ill-nature (Pro 2:15; Pro 3:32) of despising Him and His law.

bsb.text: He who walks in uprightness fears the LORD, but the one who is devious in his ways despises Him.

explanation.text: rod of pride--that is, the punishment of pride, which they evince by their words. The words of the wise procure good to them.

bsb.text: The proud speech of a fool brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.

explanation.text: crib is clean--empty; so "cleanness of teeth" denotes want of food (compare Amo 4:6). Men get the proper fruit of their doings (Gal 6:7).

bsb.text: Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty, but an abundant harvest comes through the strength of the ox.

explanation.text:
A faithful witness, etc.--one tested to be such.

utter lies--or, "breathe out lies"--that is, habitually lies (Pro 6:19; compare Act 9:1). Or the sense is, that habitual truthfulness, or lying, will be evinced in witness-bearing.

bsb.text: An honest witness does not deceive, but a dishonest witness pours forth lies.

explanation.text: An humble, teachable spirit succeeds in seeking (Pro 8:9; Joh 7:17; Jam 1:5-6).

bsb.text: A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.

explanation.text: Avoid the society of those who cannot teach you.

bsb.text: Stay away from a foolish man; you will gain no knowledge from his speech.

explanation.text: Appearances deceive the thoughtless, but the prudent discriminate.

bsb.text: The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way, but the folly of fools deceives them.

explanation.text:
Fools make a mock at sin--or, "Sin deludes fools."

righteous . . . favour--that is, of God, instead of the punishment of sin.

bsb.text: Fools mock the making of amends, but goodwill is found among the upright.

explanation.text: Each one best knows his own sorrows or joys.

bsb.text: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares in its joy.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 12:7). The contrast of the whole is enhanced by that of house and tabernacle, a permanent and a temporary dwelling.

bsb.text: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.

explanation.text:
end thereof--or, "reward," what results (compare Pro 5:4).

ways of death--leading to it.

bsb.text: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.

explanation.text: The preceding sentiment illustrated by the disappointments of a wicked or untimely joy.

bsb.text: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in sorrow.

explanation.text:
filled . . . ways--receive retribution (Pro 1:31).

a good man . . . himself--literally, "is away from such," will not associate with him.

bsb.text: The backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways, but a good man is rewarded for his ways.

explanation.text: The simple . . . word--He is credulous, not from love, but heedlessness (Pro 13:16).

bsb.text: The simple man believes every word, but the prudent man watches his steps.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 3:7; Pro 28:14).

rageth--acts proudly and conceitedly.

bsb.text: A wise man fears and turns from evil, but a fool is careless and reckless.

explanation.text:
He . . . angry--literally, "short of anger" (compare Pro 14:29, opposite idea).

man . . . hated--that is, the deliberate evildoer is more hated than the rash.

bsb.text: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, and a devious man is hated.

explanation.text:
inherit--as a portion (compare Pro 3:35).

are crowned--literally, "are surrounded with it," abound in it.

bsb.text: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

explanation.text: Describes the humbling of the wicked by the punishment their sins incur.

bsb.text: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

explanation.text: This sad but true picture of human nature is not given approvingly, but only as a fact.

bsb.text: The poor man is hated even by his neighbor, but many are those who love the rich.

explanation.text: For such contempt of the poor is contrasted as sinful with the virtuous compassion of the good.

bsb.text: He who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is he who shows kindness to the poor.

explanation.text:
As usual, the interrogative negative strengthens the affirmative.

mercy and truth--that is, God's (Psa 57:3; Psa 61:7).

bsb.text: Do not those who contrive evil go astray? But those who plan goodness find loving devotion and faithfulness.

explanation.text:
labour--painful diligence.

talk . . . penury--idle and vain promises and plans.

bsb.text: There is profit in all labor, but mere talk leads only to poverty.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 3:16).

foolishness . . . folly--Folly remains, or produces folly; it has no benefit.

bsb.text: The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the effort of fools is folly.

explanation.text:
Life often depends on truth-telling.

a deceitful . . . lies--He that breathes out lies is deceit, not to be trusted (Pro 14:5).

bsb.text: A truthful witness saves lives, but one who utters lies is deceitful.

explanation.text: The blessings of piety descend to children (Pro 13:22; Pro 20:7; Exo 20:6).

bsb.text: He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 13:14).

fear of the Lord--or, "law of the wise," is wisdom (Psa 111:10).

bsb.text: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man from the snares of death.

explanation.text: The teaching of a true political economy.

bsb.text: A large population is a king’s splendor, but a lack of subjects is a prince’s ruin.

explanation.text:
slow . . . understanding--(Compare Pro 14:17).

hasty--(Compare Pro 14:17).

exalteth folly--makes it conspicuous, as if delighting to honor it.

bsb.text: A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man promotes folly.

explanation.text: A sound heart--both literally and figuratively, a source of health; in the latter sense, opposed to the known effect of evil passions on health.

bsb.text: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.

explanation.text: reproacheth his Maker--who is the God of such, as well as of the rich (Pro 22:2; Job 31:15; and specially Sa1 2:8; Psa 113:7).

bsb.text: Whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.

explanation.text:
driven--thrust out violently (compare Psa 35:5-6).

hath hope--trusteth (Pro 10:2; Pro 11:4; Psa 2:12), implying assurance of help.

bsb.text: The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.

explanation.text: resteth--preserved in quietness for use, while fools blazon their folly (Pro 12:23; Pro 13:16).

bsb.text: Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning; even among fools she is known.

explanation.text:
Righteousness--just principles and actions.

exalteth--raises to honor.

is a reproach--brings on them the ill-will of others (compare Pro 13:6).

bsb.text: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.

explanation.text:
wise--discreet or prudent.

causeth shame-- (Pro 10:5; Pro 12:4) acts basely.

Next: Proverbs Chapter 15

bsb.text: A king delights in a wise servant, but his anger falls on the shameful.
